title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is handwritten on the verso of a typed page, whose mirrored text shows through. It does not continue the Récoltes et Semailles footnotes (Kashiwara/Mebkhout) on the neighbouring pages. It is a short, self-contained scrap of order-theoretic and Boolean-algebra reasoning, apparently part of a small investigation of when a structure Σ with a binary relation ('disjointness', written a|b) behaves like, or is, a Boolean algebra. The earlier statements it cites (Lemma 1 or 2, Cor. 1 (iii)) are not on this page.

Corollary 2, first statement. Let α, β be nonzero, α∨β ≠ 1, and γ = C(α∨β), the complement, so γ ≠ 0. Under the (equivalent) conditions of Cor. 1 (iii), α, β, γ form a 'base' of the Boolean subalgebra generated by α and β. 'Base' means the atoms: pairwise disjoint and joining to 1. This is correct exactly when α∧β = 0. Presumably Cor. 1 (iii) is a disjointness hypothesis α|β; otherwise the atoms would be α∧Cβ, α∧β, Cα∧β and γ.

Corollary 2, second statement. Under the conditions of Lemma 2, with 0 < b < c < 1, put α = b, β = c∧Cb, γ = Cc. Then α, β, γ are the atoms of the Boolean algebra generated by b and c. This is standard: a chain 0 < b < c < 1 induces the partition b, c∖b, 1∖c, which generates the 8-element algebra.

Questions.
(1) Are the conditions of Lemma 1 / Cor. 1 on Σ always satisfied, or at least when Σ is finite? A marginal note answers: no, there is a counterexample with card Σ = 10. The example itself is not given.
(2) If these conditions are satisfied, is Σ necessarily a Boolean algebra?
(3) Can one impose an analogue of the Cor. 1 (iii) hypothesis for arbitrary, possibly infinite, families (x_i)_{i∈I} of mutually disjoint elements? This is a completeness or σ-additivity type axiom.
(4) One should determine exactly what the conditions amount to when Σ comes from an ordered set L, with the relation a|b iff x<y or y<x, i.e. the comparability relation.

Overall, this looks like an attempt to characterise Boolean algebras, or recover Boolean structure, from a binary 'disjointness/orthogonality' or comparability relation. That is close in spirit to orthogonality spaces, test spaces and orthoposets in quantum logic, and to comparability graphs of posets. The purpose within the 1986 'Ateliers' notes is unclear from this page alone.
errors: The first statement of Corollary 2 (α, β, γ = C(α∨β) form the atoms of the generated Boolean algebra) is true only if α∧β = 0. Presumably this is supplied by the hypotheses of Cor. 1 (iii), which are not visible here; as written on this page alone it is a gap.
The counterexample with card Σ = 10 is asserted in the margin but not given, so it cannot be checked.

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks exactly which axioms on a disjointness/comparability relation force Boolean-algebra structure, including in the case where the relation is the comparability relation of a poset L. He notes a 10-element counterexample showing his conditions are not automatic. The thread is left open.
missed.quote: Il faudrait déterminer exactement les conditions qui en sont, quand Σ est défini via un ens. ordonné L, avec la relation a|b ssi x<y ou y<x.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only marginally. Such questions are largely covered by the existing literature on orthogonality spaces and comparability graphs. The counterexample and the specific axioms (lost Cor. 1/Lemma 1) are not recoverable from this page.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary Boolean-algebra facts plus open-ended axiomatisation questions whose context is missing. Similar questions are standard in quantum logic and in comparability-graph theory. It is mildly curious biographically: an isolated combinatorial scrap amid 1986 Récoltes et Semailles footnotes.
transcription_corrections: Top line: 'Sous les conditions (équivalentes) du Cor. 1 (iii),' — the inserted word is 'éq.' for 'équivalentes', placed above 'conditions'.

'Les conditions envisagées au Lemme Σ [?] Cor. 1 sur Σ' should read roughly 'Les conditions envisagées au Lemme 1 et Cor. 1 sur Σ sont-elles toujours vérifiées ? (une demande faite de la ...), ou si Σ est fini ?'
'pour les familles (x_i)_{i∈I} d'éléments mutuellement disjoints de I' should be '... disjoints de Σ, I non nécessairement fini'.

Last lines: 'Il faudrait déterminer exactement les conditions qui en sont, quand Σ est défini via un ens. ordonné L, avec la relation a|b ssi x<y ou y<x' — 'via un ens. ordonné', not 'via une [?] ordonné'; 'avec', not 'mais de'.
Margin note: 'Non, a-t-on contre-exemple avec card Σ = 10' — this is a marginal answer to the first question, not part of the main text.
